data.name: Chhaya
data.gender_notes: Chhaya is used as a female name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit chāyā, 'shadow, shade, reflection'. Its root is Sanskrit chāyā (छाया). A classical Sanskrit term; also a goddess. Chhaya is a Sanskrit name meaning “Shadow; shade; reflection”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Chhaya expresses “Shadow; shade; reflection”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit chāyā, 'shadow, shade, reflection'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chhaya total 28, reducing to 1. Number 1 is associated with leadership, independence and initiative.

vedic_reference.note: The name Chhaya is derived from the Sanskrit word 'च्छय' (chhaya) which means 'shadow'. In Hindu mythology, Chhaya is the goddess of shadows and is often depicted as the wife of the god Indra. She is also known as the goddess of beauty and grace.

historical_references.reference: A classical Sanskrit term; also a goddess.
